newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ansett in Sydney Olympics airline alliance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ansett in Sydney Olympics airline alliance.

text.p: Ansett Airlines Ltd said on Monday it had formed a global airline alliance with six other airlines to be the official airline carrier for the Sydney 2000 Olympics.
The Global Airline Team, comprises Ansett, Air New Zealand Ltd, Deutsche Lufthansa Ag, Malaysian Airline System Bhd, South African Airways, Thai Airways International and United Airlines.
Ansett's newly-appointed executive chairman Rod Eddington said the partners had a potential to gain about A$1.5 billion in extra revenue from the alliance formation.
"Over a four year period there is a really good opportunity for in excess of A$1.5 billion," Eddington told reporters after being asked about revenue forecasts for the alliance.
"That is broken down into many forms and ways, but overall there is enormous market opportunity to bring people to Australia and there is also domestic revenue opportunity," Eddington said.

He said the alliance partners would invest about A$50 million in the new alliance. "The investment in cash and in kind is about A$50 million," he said. But he would break down the amounts invested by each airline.

"This is the first time in the history of the Olympics that an alliance of this character had ever been brought together before," said Mal Hemmerling, chief executive officer of the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG).
"The international Olympic movement at large are absolutely estatic that it has happened," Hemmerling told reporters.
Hemmerling said the alliance would be the official carrier of all the 2000 Games athletes and officials.
Glenn Robertson, Ansett's general manager for the Olympic Games, said the alliance estimated that the Olympics could generate an extra 950,000 passengers for the alliance.
Ansett is jointly owned by Air New Zealand and News Corp Ltd .
